taxpayer.notes: Incarcerated from February 16, 2017 through trial; resided in Kentucky when Petition filed (February 25, 2021). No 2016 or 2017 return filed; IRS prepared SFR under §6020(b) around March 9, 2020. Appeal lies to Sixth Circuit.

adjustments: included taxable life insurance distributions of $13,214 and $5,366 reported on Forms 1099-R by Prudential
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Taxability of lapsed-policy distributions in 2017; Schedule E rental loss on Signal Mountain Property claimed on proposed return; additions to tax
conceded: Petitioner conceded $500/month rent to his daughter was significantly below fair market rental value
Petitioner conceded at trial that his claimed rental loss was limited to $25,000 (§469(i))

findings_of_fact.snippet: On February 16, 2017, petitioner was incarcerated. He remained incarcerated through the time of trial.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner resided at Signal Mountain Property through February 16, 2017; vacant until September 15, 2017; rented to daughter $500/month from September 15 through year end
findings_of_fact.snippet: As of that date through the end of 2017, petitioner rented the Signal Mountain Property to his daughter for $500 per month.

findings_of_fact.fact: Policies lapsed in 2017 after premiums stopped; Prudential applied cash values to repay loans plus interest; Forms 1099-R reported taxable $13,214 and $5,366 (loan repaid by cash value less total premiums paid)
findings_of_fact.snippet: The amounts reported as taxable on the Forms 1099–R were $13,214 and $5,366,

findings_of_fact.fact: Proposed 2017 return claimed Schedule E loss of $77,675: insurance $1,762, repairs $650, utilities $3,670 (Jan 1-Sep 15), depreciation $73,593 (seven-year table); no documentation
findings_of_fact.snippet: The proposed return claimed a rental real estate loss deduction of $77,675 in connection with the Signal Mountain Property.

findings_of_fact.fact: No 2017 or 2016 return filed and no estimated tax payments for 2017
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner failed to file an income tax return for the 2017 tax year and to make estimated tax payments

findings_of_fact.fact: SFR prepared under §6020(b) on or around March 9, 2020; notice of deficiency November 30, 2020
findings_of_fact.snippet: On or around March 9, 2020, the IRS prepared a substitute for return (SFR) pursuant to section 6020(b) for petitioner’s 2017 tax year.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner's only excuse was ignorance of filing/paying requirement while incarcerated; he knew of a general duty to file
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner testified that he had “no valid excuse” for not having filed except for ignorance of the requirement to file while incarcerated.

issues.question: Other (life insurance §72(e)): Did petitioner receive taxable constructive distributions of $13,214 and $5,366 in 2017 when his two Prudential policies lapsed and cash values were applied to policy loans?
issues.holding: Yes; termination applied cash values against the loans, a constructive distribution includible to the extent it exceeds investment in the contract (premiums paid)
issues.computable_reason: Loan extinguished by cash value minus premiums paid; undisputed amounts; legal rule on timing

issues.question: Other (rental expenses / vacation home §280A): Is petitioner entitled to deduct Schedule E expenses for the Signal Mountain Property for 2017?
issues.holding: No; personal use (January 1-February 16 residence plus below-FMV rental to daughter) exceeded the greater of 14 days or 10% of fair rental days, so the dwelling was a residence and no deductions are allowed

amount_determined.description: Schedule E loss claimed and disallowed

issues.computable_reason: Day-count test of §280A(d)(1) from found dates and below-FMV rental to family member

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the section 6651(a)(1) addition to tax for failure to file a 2017 return?
issues.holding: Yes; return required and not filed; incarceration and ignorance are not reasonable cause
issues.computable_reason: Turns on rejection of reasonable cause defense

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the section 6651(a)(2) addition to tax for failure to pay the amount shown on the SFR?
issues.holding: Yes; valid §6020(b) SFR and nonpayment shown; incarceration not reasonable cause
issues.computable_reason: Turns on rejection of reasonable cause defense

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the section 6654 addition to tax for failure to pay estimated tax for 2017?
issues.holding: Yes; tax liability for 2017, no 2016 or 2017 return, no estimated payments; no general reasonable cause exception
issues.computable_reason: Mechanical: required annual payment = 90% of 2017 tax (no 2016 return); no payments; no reasonable cause exception

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Life insurance income included; Schedule E deductions disallowed under §280A; additions under 6651(a)(1), 6651(a)(2) and 6654 sustained

notes: Amounts rounded to nearest dollar. Forms 1099-R not in evidence but undisputed. Derived: personal residence days Jan 1-Feb 16, 2017 = 47 days (> 14). Respondent's alternative arguments (substantiation, depreciation basis/period, §469) not reached. Rule 155 computation needed because concessions affect amounts.
